verdict: Lend selectively to Haldia port-linked contractors and service providers with dredging-linked or SMPK-anchored cash flows; avoid pure barge/cargo intermediaries with no contracted revenue.
title: Haldia Ports & Port Services: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Haldia port services are a throughput-and-dredging business: cash comes from moving cargo and keeping the Hooghly channel deep enough for ships.** The Haldia Dock Complex needs maintenance dredging along a 125-km stretch, and silt accumulation restricts larger vessels [2]. The Centre has sanctioned ₹430.7 crore for dredging at Kolkata and Haldia [3], with ₹430 crore reported for Kolkata Port dredging [1]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's revenue is tied to dredging contracts, cargo handling, or neither; if neither, ask what physical asset or contract generates the cash.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits with whoever holds the dredging or handling contract; cash sits upstream of the borrower.** From 2026-27, SMPK must meet performance targets on PPP cargo volume, facility modernisation, throughput growth and earnings before tax excluding subsidy to qualify for central assistance [2]. Central dredging support is to be phased down, with SMPK meeting the entire expenditure from internal resources after 2030-31 [2]. So when a proposal lands, check the borrower's contract tenure against that 2030-31 taper; if the contract ends before it, ask how renewal is secured.

## What has changed now
**The news is a funding positive but a discipline test for the port authority, not automatic comfort for its vendors.** Peer results show volume momentum: Adani Ports Q2 FY27 profit rose 16.5% to ₹3,622 crore on revenue of ₹11,340 crore, with EBITDA margin at 60% [5][6]. But a peer-sector report flags cost inflation offsetting volume growth in Q2FY27 [7]. Rating reports on port/logistics peers show receivable periods of 60 days [8] and 57 days [11], and operating cycles of 51 days [9]. These are peer benchmarks, not Haldia data; collect from customer for local receivable days.

## Who to pursue and how to grow safely
**Pursue dredging contractors, PPP cargo-handling operators and equipment/service vendors with SMPK-linked or multi-year contracts; avoid one-client barge operators and pure cargo intermediaries.** Structure against assigned contract receivables, keep tenor inside contract life, and take monthly throughput or cargo-volume statements plus receivable-ageing. If receivable days drift past the peer 60-day mark [8], ask for the SMPK payment trail.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for contract concentration, delayed SMPK payments and capex funded on hope of renewal.** If a borrower's order book depends on one SMPK tender, ask for the award letter and payment history. If dredging spend shifts to internal resources after 2030-31 [2], vendors exposed to that line need a diversification plan. Local Haldia-specific data is thin in these sources; lean on first principles and the peer benchmarks above.
watch: Days cross 60 [8] -> ask for SMPK payment trail and reprice
Single-client share above half -> seek assignment or reduce limit
Volumes fall two quarters running -> freeze fresh limits
Dredging shifted to internal funds [2] -> review vendor exposure
